outcomes.text: Record personal experiences and observations using first-hand sources, secondary sources and individual research.
Gather, document and respond to visual information through varied techniques.
Select, contextualise and organise collected information coherently.
Use diverse resources effectively to develop artistic practice.
Undertake personal investigations.
Apply varied skills to create art and design work.
Assess, revise and edit their own work.
Reflect on work, then refine and adapt it.
Research visually through direct and secondary sources, recording observations, experiences and developing ideas appropriately.
Experiment with photographic techniques including focus range, lighting, exposure, viewpoint, composition, framing and editing.
Experiment with photographic media and processes, including film, pinhole, photograms, multiple exposures, scanning and digital manipulation.
Explore hand-drawn, stop-motion and digital animation media and processes for animation, film or game design.
Select, evaluate and improve work throughout development to create a personal response.
Create storyboards and images using photography, models, drawing or illustration.
Understand photographic conventions and genres including portraiture, landscape and documentary.
Respond creatively to a theme or brief.
Consider the intended audience for photographic, animation, film or game-design work.
Understand different types and genres of photography and animation.
Understand suitable photographic or animation materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Understand how intention, research, realisation and reflection support relevant creative processes.
Know a range of relevant artists, photographers and animators.
